Finally, studies in MLCK knock-out mice confirm that this myeloid-driven pathology requires MLCK-dependent tight junction opening for paracellular neutrophil migration, which works in concert with LAP-TLR2 signaling during Lm-induced gastroenteritis.
nef9360ad19f3: Local Jacobians of single-cell dynamics are used to locate unstable cells along trajectories, but what they identify from measured data has rarely been tested against independent truth. We present scJDO2, which separates two per-cell operators by the time information they require: a score operator, the Hessian of a score-matched log density, available from any snapshot; and a flow operator, the Jacobian of a drift fitted to a measured velocity, here estimated label-free from a sampled time course by entropic optimal transport. Both are summarized in a shared operator space of magnitude-free descriptors, with the invariance of each stated, and evaluated with pre-registered tests. On synthetic data calibrated to six real datasets, the flow operator from the time course alone separated fate-bifurcation cells from committed cells on held-out seeds (AUC 0.89-1.00) with a-priori settings; tuning on development seeds overfit. On LARRY lineage-traced hematopoiesis, its fitted drift predicted the clonal displacement of barcoded cells beyond population movement (Spearman 0.56, permutation p < 0.001; 0.50 after removing the mean shift) and a held-out sampling day better than mean-displacement and no-movement baselines (energy distance 0.69, 95 % CI 0.66-0.73, vs 0.87 and 0.88); lineage thus validates the velocity, not {lambda}. Mini-batch transport reproduced dense transport (velocity cosine 0.9998) and scaled to all 130,887 cells (transport 5 min and 2.5 GB; drift fit and Jacobians 21 min and 1.3 GB). On an independent simulator it detected two of three bifurcations and two of three cycles and never reported instability on linear trajectories. Several readings failed. Neither operator recovers the values of the true Jacobian; the flow operators leading eigenvalue ranks branching cells empirically. The flow operator depends on the transport metric and inverts on Factor Analysis. Operator archetypes isolated bifurcation cells but did not outperform expression clustering and were unstable across fit seeds. The score operator did not predict CRISPRi knockdown responses or sister-cell fate coherence. A confirmatory test of transition timing could not be constructed, and diffusion is not identifiable at typical sampling intervals. The released software reports these diagnostics.
n0ffdc631f771: Clinical electrocardiography is organized as a structured set of correlated leads, yet most neural ECG classifiers assume that all twelve leads are present, correctly ordered, and acquired under the same device conditions at training and deployment. We propose LeadWeaver, a topology-aware ECG representation model designed for diagnosis under missing, corrupted, or device-shifted leads. LeadWeaver represents each lead as a temporal token stream, couples leads through a fixed-plus-learned physiological lead graph, and performs masked-lead latent completion rather than waveform synthesis. A reliability router estimates which observed leads should dominate each diagnostic decision, while a consistency objective aligns complete-lead and incomplete-lead predictions. We evaluate the model on PTB-XL and CPSC-style settings using complete-input diagnosis, arbitrary missing-lead subsets, lead corruption, cross-dataset transfer, calibration, and selective prediction. The central hypothesis is that robust ECG diagnosis requires explicitly modeling both inter-lead topology and uncertainty about unavailable evidence, rather than treating missing channels as zero-valued inputs. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.
n6a1c1f927900: Variation in primate olfactory receptor gene repertoires has been linked to shared ecological and sensory drivers, including diet, diurnality, and colour vision. Yet within anthropoids, each link rests on a single lineage, leaving unclear whether this variation reflects a shared response to these drivers or lineage-specific histories. Here, we combine genomic data from 80 New World monkey species with CT-based olfactory anatomy and ecological data to investigate the evolutionary processes underlying repertoire variation. Ecological and sensory variables explain little of this variation; even routinely trichromatic, leaf-eating howler monkeys have repertoires of unremarkable size. Instead, convergent reductions in repertoire size arose through distinct genomic routes: extensive gene inactivation in titi monkeys and large structural deletions in squirrel monkeys. Owl monkeys, the only anthropoids that reverted to nocturnality, retained rather than expanded a large ancestral repertoire shared with diurnal capuchins, and instead enlarged their olfactory bulb. Repertoire size covaries with olfactory bulb volume across the radiation, but only partially within lineages: squirrel monkeys show the converse, losing receptors without a matching bulb reduction. Thus, olfactory evolution in New World monkeys reflects historical contingency rather than a shared response, with convergent changes in repertoire size and partial decoupling of genomic and anatomical evolution.
n41bae9bb9680: Background: Early diagnostic triage for suspected dengue is important in high-volume settings, yet confirmatory testing may be delayed or intermittently available. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a simple complete blood count (CBC)-derived score to estimate the likelihood of same-day dengue non-structural protein 1 (NS1) antigen positivity among suspected dengue patients in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Methods: We conducted a retrospective model-development study at Uttara Adhunik Medical College Hospital using data from patients with clinical suspicion of dengue between 19 August and 12 October 2023. The final analysis included 596 unique patients who underwent CBC and NS1 testing on the same day. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) penalized logistic regression was used for variable selection among routinely available demographic and hematological predictors. Selected predictors were refit using unpenalized logistic regression to derive a CBC score. Internal validation and calibration were assessed using bootstrap optimism correction with 400 resamples. Results: Among 596 patients, 306 (51.3%) were NS1 positive. The final parsimonious model retained platelet count rescaled per 10 x 109/L, white blood cell count, and monocyte count. The optimism-corrected AUC was 0.9429. At the Youden-derived cutoff of 11.825, the final integer score had sensitivity 0.833 (95% CI, 0.787-0.873), specificity 0.966 (95% CI, 0.938-0.983), PPV 0.962 (95% CI, 0.932-0.982), NPV 0.846 (95% CI, 0.802-0.883), and accuracy 0.898 (95% CI, 0.870-0.921). A rounded cutoff of 12 produced similar performance. In benchmark analysis, the final model showed a modest improvement over platelet count alone (AUC 0.944 vs 0.931; Delta AUC 0.012; DeLong p=0.00364). Conclusion: A three-parameter CBC score can estimate the likelihood of NS1 antigen positivity among suspected dengue patients in this single-center dataset. The score should be interpreted as a CBC-only triage adjunct, not as a replacement for confirmatory dengue testing. External validation in independent cohorts is needed before routine clinical use.
n74f406be9462: Typing dynamics are being investigated as a digital behavioral marker for Parkinson's disease (PD), but the cross-dataset reliability of typing-based classi ers remains uncertain. We evaluated four public datasets (475 par ticipants; 270 with PD and 205 controls) across 12 transfer directions using split conformal prediction targeting 90% marginal coverage. In all three pri mary directions, coverage was below the 0.90 target and the one-sided tests remained signi cant after Holm correction: 0.598 (95% CI, 0.4830.704) for Tappy[->]MIT, 0.850 (0.7880.899) for MIT[->]Tappy, and 0.732 (0.6840.777) for clinical[->]self-reported transfer. Discrimination and coverage did not con sistently change together: LightGBM had lower AUC than logistic regression in all 12 directions but higher coverage in 11, with larger prediction sets. Class-conditional coverage varied by target cohort: PD-conditional cover age was 0.214 for Tappy[->]MIT, whereas healthy-control coverage was 0.700 for MIT[->]Tappy and 0.627 for clinical[->]self-reported transfer. Recalibration with 9 and 18 labeled target participants raised the lower condence bound above 0.80 in the latter two directions; in Tappy[->]MIT, it remained below 0.80 even with 25 labels. Weighted conformal prediction yielded coverage of 0.9181.000 without target labels but returned the full label set for 86% 100% of participants. Stress tests did not reproduce the observed coverage patterns, and black-box shift estimation did not support pure label shift as the dominant explanation for Tappy[->]MIT. Evaluating typing dynamics as a digital marker for PD requires cross-dataset assessment of discrimination, marginal and class-conditional coverage, and recovery costs. Clinical screen ing utility has not been established.
n6a6fdfbe8f8f: Background. As kidneys age, their cells change in arrangement and gene expression. Whether these changes are also present in diabetic kidney disease (DKD), and whether they relate to how quickly kidney function is lost, is not known. Methods. Zero-time biopsies from 24 healthy living kidney donors (aged 36-66 years) and biopsies from 28 patients with DKD were profiled by single-cell-level spatial transcriptomics with a 5,101-gene panel. In the donors, we identified how cell neighborhoods and cell-type gene expression change with age and summarized the expression changes as tissue-aging scores. The scores were applied unchanged to DKD and related to the rate of eGFR decline after biopsy in 24 patients, with adjustment for age, sex, baseline eGFR, and proteinuria. We also estimated the scores from routine periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) slides, using models that did not include the patient being scored. Results. In older donors, immune cells were less often found next to tubular epithelium, and contacts between endothelial cells and podocytes and between stromal and epithelial cells were fewer, although cell proportions changed little. Expression of stress-response and cell-cycle regulators (FOXO3, CDKN1A, BBC3, PINK1, IRAK1, SOCS1) increased. Changes in cell contacts in DKD tissue largely followed the same direction as those in older donors. In DKD, higher tissue-aging scores were associated with faster eGFR loss independently of age, sex, baseline eGFR, and proteinuria (overall score, partial {rho} = -0.61); this held for tubular, endothelial, immune, and parietal epithelial cell scores but not for the podocyte score. Scores estimated from PAS slides correlated with the transcriptomic scores (mean {rho} = 0.62) and were also associated with faster eGFR loss (partial {rho}, -0.44 to -0.56). Conclusions. Healthy kidney aging involves a selective loss of cell contacts together with a coordinated stress-response program. DKD kidneys that carry this aging phenotype lose function faster, and the phenotype can be estimated in part from the routine diagnostic PAS slide.
nde6fdaa20203: Background: Although direct-acting antivirals have transformed hepatitis C virus (HCV) treatment, 25-30% of active infections in Spain remain undiagnosed. We aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine-learning model to identify undiagnosed HCV infection using only data already recorded within the health system. Materials and Methods: We conducted a retrospective, population-based cohort study using the Andalusian Population Health Database (BPS). Individuals diagnosed with HCV between 2017 and 2024 (n=25,028) were matched, up to 10:1, to controls by birth year, sex, and health district. An Explainable Boosting Machine was trained on 2017-2022 data, with a threshold set in a 2023 validation set to guarantee [≥]60% sensitivity, then evaluated unmodified in an independent, non-matched, population-representative 2024 sample approximating real-world screening. Predictors comprised chronic-disease diagnoses and laboratory summary statistics recorded [≥]30 days before the index date; age and sex were excluded as matching variables. Predictors reflecting socioeconomic proxies or matching artefacts (pharmaceutical co-payment category, a zone-level deprivation index) were removed after explainability review. Results: In the independent test set, the model achieved an AUC of 0.837 (0.826 in validation), sensitivity 63.5%, specificity 91.8%, positive predictive value 7.0%, and negative predictive value 99.6%. Leading predictors were minimum alanine aminotransferase, HIV infection, dependence on non-tobacco substances, and platelet-count statistics, forming a clinically coherent, laboratory- and comorbidity-driven profile. Conclusion: An explainable model built exclusively from routine electronic health record data can identify undiagnosed HCV infection with discrimination comparable to previously published tools, evaluated under conditions approximating true population prevalence. Bias-auditing was feasible without sacrificing interpretability, supporting a scalable, equity-conscious instrument for the final phase of HCV elimination.
n5407ef455f8b: Importance: Severe anorexia nervosa (AN) carries substantial mortality risk, but its consequences associated with social and occupational functioning remain poorly characterized, limiting the development of targeted interventions to improve functioning, prevent and reduce long-term social disadvantage. Objective: To determine whether AN severity is associated with educational attainment, employment, income, and cohabitation status. Design: Cohort study following social and occupational outcomes across adulthood until age 55. Setting: Population-based. Participants: All individuals born in Denmark from 1963 to 1994, alive and residing in Denmark at age 30. The AN group had a first AN diagnosis between ages 10 and 25 years, excluding those who died or emigrated within 5 years. The comparison group had no AN diagnosis. Exposure: Illness severity of AN, measured by the AN Register-based Severity Index 5 years after the first AN diagnosis. Main Outcomes and Measures: Educational attainment was assessed at age 25 (upper secondary education) and at age 30/35 (highest completed education). Employment status, income deficiency, and cohabitation status were assessed annually from age 30 to 55. Results: Among 2,442,916 individuals, 9,465 were diagnosed with AN, of whom 1,996 (21.1%) were classified as severe AN cases. At age 25, individuals with severe AN had increased odds of non-completion of upper-secondary education compared to the general population (odds ratio [OR]=3.07; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.72-3.46), and those with less severe AN (OR=1.39; 95% CI: 1.29-1.50). At age 30, severe AN was associated with higher odds of unemployment (OR=3.42; 95% CI: 3.03-3.86), income deficiency (OR=3.84; 95% CI: 3.42-4.31), and living alone (OR=2.43; 95% CI: 2.17-2.71) compared to the less severe AN group. The risk of unemployment and income deficiency diverged across time: individuals with less severe AN gradually approached the general population, whereas those with severe AN diverged further over time. Within the AN cohort, severity differences persisted after adjustment for active AN diagnosis, with minimal attenuation. Conclusions and Relevance: Greater lifetime AN severity was associated with significantly poorer long-term social and occupational functioning outcomes, and these functional difficulties may persist beyond periods of active illness. This vulnerable group needs substantial support in these areas throughout the course of illness.
n8a1c946fdcd5: Maternal mental illness affects roughly one in five mothers in the United States, yet most evidence linking it to the mother-child relationship comes from the first postpartum year and relies on self-report measures of depression, anxiety, and stress. In 613 women spanning five family contexts - pregnancy and mothers whose youngest child was aged 0-2, 3-12, 13-17, or 18 and older - we examined twelve psychological constructs as correlates of mothers' relational reports. Eleven were associated with relational reports individually; entered together, only three retained independent associations surviving false discovery rate correction: cross-domain psychiatric symptom burden (beta = 0.38), delay discounting (beta = -0.11), and orienting sensitivity (beta = 0.10). To our knowledge, this is the first peer-reviewed study linking delay discounting to maternal relational reports. Depression, anxiety, anger, perceived stress, and negative affect fell to non-significance, and the symptom composite that displaced them contains none of those domains, indicating that breadth of psychiatric symptoms, not their type, tracked relational reports. A person-centered analysis converged: the latent profile with the poorest relational reports was defined by symptoms across multiple domains rather than by elevated stress alone. Associations varied across family contexts, though because each context used a different relational instrument, differences cannot be attributed to child age. These cross-sectional findings suggest that the psychological dimension most closely tied to maternal relational reports is broader than the perinatal mood constructs around which research and screening are organized, and that cross-domain symptom assessment warrants prospective evaluation as a complement to mood screening.
nc6986656edb4: Objective: To develop and evaluate a biomarker-informed, computable phenotype of the heart failure (HF) continuum, aligned with 2026 AHA/ACC/ESC/WHF Expert Consensus, using NHANES and linked mortality data, and to determine whether this phenotype identifies subgroups with distinct mortality risks. Methods: We analyzed 11,477 U.S. adults aged [≥]20 years from the 1999-2004 NHANES cycles who participated in the surplus-sera biomarker substudy and were linked to National Death Index follow-up. Participants were classified into four phenotypes according to the 2026 Universal Definition of Heart Failure: no apparent risk, Stage A (at risk), Stage B (elevated NT-proBNP without self-reported HF), and Stage C (self-reported HF). Survey-weighted Kaplan-Meier curves and nested, multiply imputed Cox proportional hazards models, with sequential adjustment for demographic, socioeconomic, and cardiometabolic covariates, were used to estimate associations with mortality. Pairwise phenotype comparisons, standardized adjusted survival estimates, and restricted mean survival times were also calculated. Incremental prognostic value was evaluated by comparing discrimination and reclassification metrics between the full phenotype and a conventional three-level model that excluded NT-proBNP. Results: Weighted prevalences were 16.9%, 70.0%, 10.7%, and 2.4% for no apparent risk, Stage A, Stage B, and Stage C, respectively. In fully adjusted models, the hazard ratios (HRs) relative to no apparent risk were 1.58 (95% CI, 1.08-2.30), 2.88 (95% CI, 2.00-4.16), and 2.56 (95% CI, 1.61-4.09), respectively. Stage B was associated with significantly higher mortality risk than Stage A (HR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.62-2.07), whereas the difference between Stage C and Stage B was not statistically significant (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.71-1.11). The association for Stage B attenuated less across sequentially adjusted models than that for Stage C. Adjusted 10-year mortality risks were 15.2% for Stage B and 14.2% for Stage C. Incorporating Stage B into the conventional model yielded only marginal improvements in discrimination ({Delta}C-statistic, 0.002; 95% CI, 0.001-0.002). Conclusion: A biomarker-informed phenotype of the HF continuum can be operationalized using national survey data and identifies a pre-HF subgroup with an adjusted mortality risk not significantly different from that of individuals with overt HF, despite only marginal gains in prognostic discrimination.
n1b291d1bbc47: Background: Despite increasing interest in the gut-brain axis, the role of the autonomic nervous system and the brainstem in human gut-brain signalling remain largely unknown. Objective: To characterise resting state functional connectivity (FC) of the brainstem in healthy older adults and to examine its association with a variety of factors relevant to ageing and the gut-brain axis, and to assess if brainstem FC is altered by probiotic intervention. Design: Randomised, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial in 60-80-year-olds (55 women/28 men) with six-weeks Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus HN001 intervention in a non-encapsulated and microencapsulated formulation. Brainstem-optimised functional magnetic resonance imaging was performed before and after intervention. Results: At baseline, age correlated positively with FC of locus coeruleus (LC) and dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) with pre-/postcentral gyrus, as well as of periaqueductal gray (PAG) with temporal/supramarginal gyrus and planum temporale. FC of PAG with precuneus cortex and cingulate gyrus correlated with cognitive status and mood. Perceived stress correlated with FC between nucleus tractus solitarius and occipital cortex, angular/temporal gyrus. FC of DRN differed between men and women. All p<0.0063. Following probiotic intervention, a significant time*group interaction and main time effect were observed for FC of LC and ventral tegmental area. FC of both with occipital pole/cortex and cerebellum, and of LC with pre-/postcentral gyrus, superior parietal lobule, insular/opercular cortex, putamen, and planum polare showed within-group changes (non-encapsulated), no between-group differences were observed (all p<0.0056). Conclusion: Brainstem-to-cortex FC at rest correlates with several phenotypic characteristics implicated in healthy ageing and may be modifiable by probiotic supplementation.
nb7ee1e943621: Introduction Electronic health record (EHR) data increasingly drive quality monitoring and research, yet their reliability in dentistry is uncertain. We compared the completeness, consistency, and accuracy of periodontal diagnoses captured in two different formats (structured fields versus narrative notes) across two academic dental centers sharing the same EHR platform and diagnostic terminology. Methods In this retrospective study of qualifying periodontal encounters (2021), structured diagnoses were extracted by SQL and narrative diagnoses by a fine-tuned RoBERTa NLP model. A random sample (~20%) was independently reviewed by two board-certified periodontists, with disagreements resolved by consensus, to form the gold standard. Outcomes were completeness (presence of a diagnosis), consistency (agreement between formats), and accuracy (agreement with the gold standard), with ordinal periodontal stage compared using quadratic weighted {kappa}. Results Across 4,542 encounters, completeness varied widely by site and format (34.7% - 84.5%), and neither format was consistently more complete; at one site, over one-third of encounters (35.8%) had no documented diagnosis in either format. Among dual-documented encounters, agreement between formats was substantial but imperfect ({kappa} = 0.86 and 0.80). Accuracy against the gold standard was modest for both sources (all near 50%), with narrative notes numerically higher at both sites and favored by the severity-weighted {kappa}, though raw differences were not significant. Pooled across sites, the formats diverged in 14.8% of dual-documented encounters, 8.4% by two or more stages, with the structured field carrying the milder stage in 67.9% of disagreements. Conclusions Structured and unstructured periodontal diagnoses each matched expert adjudication only about half the time, and neither was consistently more complete. Narrative notes held a small severity-weighted accuracy advantage, and coded fields more often carried the milder stage when the two disagreed. These convergent, cross-site patterns appear systematic rather than site-specific and expose latent risks for analytics and decision support. Improving dental EHR data quality will require workflows that combine the computability of coded entries with the fidelity of free text.
n9ea973c5dcb8: Background: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) and dermatomyositis (DM) are autoimmune diseases that have been proposed as models of cancer immunoediting. Autoantibody-defined subsets show divergent cancer risks, yet malignancy often remains clinically occult. We tested whether circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) can reveal subclinical cancer in new-onset SSc and DM. Methods: We prospectively recruited adults with recent SSc or DM onset. Plasma ctDNA was assessed using a targeted next-generation sequencing panel covering commonly mutated cancer genes. Patients were followed for 18-24 months on average. ctDNA positivity was correlated with subsequent cancer diagnoses. Findings: Among 134 patients (69 SSc, 65 DM), cancer was diagnosed in six (4.5%; three SSc, three DM). ctDNA was detected in four of these six patients (67%) a median of 13 months (range 1.4-17) before clinical diagnosis; in three of four patients, mutations detected in plasma matched those subsequently identified in the same patients primary tumors. ctDNA was also detected in 16 of 128 patients without a cancer diagnosis. ctDNA positivity conferred an 11.4-fold higher risk of malignancy relative to ctDNA negativity and yielded a negative predictive value of 98% and a positive predictive value of 20% for cancer within the observation window. Interpretation: ctDNA testing identified most cancers that emerged within 18 months in new-onset SSc and DM and stratified near-term cancer risk. These findings support larger, interventional trials to determine whether ctDNA-guided surveillance improves timeliness of cancer detection, optimizes imaging and biopsy strategies, and enhances outcomes in patients with SSc and DM.
n35be0a39fd20: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) exhibit heterogeneous functional decline, potentially influenced by systemic metabolic reserve. We investigate whether circulating insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) is associated with subsequent functional change in ALS. Serum IGF-1 was measured in 37 participants with ALS and 25 healthy controls. Baseline levels were compared between groups, and across disease-duration defined progression categories. Lagged regression assessed whether prior visit IGF-1 level predicted change in Revised ALS Functional Rating Scale (ALSFRS-R) on the next visit, adjusting for inter-visit interval, body mass index, age and sex. Mixed-effects and sensitivity analyses assessed robustness. Baseline IGF-1 did not differ significantly between controls and ALS (mean + SD: 107.3 + 54.3 vs 132.2 + 68.3 ng/mL, p = 0.12), or across progression categories (F(2, 34) = 0.13, p = 0.88). Across 48 intervals from 23 ALS participants, each 1-SD higher IGF-1 from prior visit was associated with 1.40-point less subsequent {Delta}ALSFRS-R decline (95% CI: 0.03 to 2.77, p = 0.045). Generalised estimating equations yielded a similar association ({beta} = 1.50, p = 0.030), whereas small-cluster robust inference showed wider uncertainty (p = 0.084). Repeated IGF-1 showed an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.69, and the lagged association remained positive in all 23 leave-one-participant-out analyses. The IGF-1-by-time interaction was not significant in a random-slope mixed model (p =0.254). Higher circulating IGF-1 may reflect systemic trophic-metabolic reserve associated with short-term functional preservation in ALS, but limited precision precludes definitive prognostic or causal conclusions.
na8b62bce90b4: Objective: We test whether data collected from daily passive smartphone sensing and self-reports can predict daily significant psychological distress with meaningful potential clinical utility, comparing across best-in-class machine learning algorithms. Methods: In this prospective cohort study, 169 community-dwelling adults completed baseline surveys followed by 7 days of passive smartphone sensing (accelerometer, GPS, power state) and end-of-day Brief Symptom Inventory-18 (BSI-18) assessments. Cases were defined as days (total n = 1,062) where participants' psychological distress measured with the sex-specific BSI-18 Global Severity Index T-score was [≥]63 (prevalence 11.2%). Four classical models (artificial neural network, elastic net, support vector machine [SVM], extreme gradient boosting [XGB]) and four transformers (sensor-only or multimodal; standard or fusion architecture) were tuned, Platt-calibrated and evaluated on held-out participants (210 records, 25 cases) with participant-level bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results: The SVM (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC] 0.84; 95% CI 0.71-0.93), the multimodal fusion transformer (0.84; 0.69-0.95) and XGB (0.82; 0.63-0.94) discriminated best; sensor-only transformers performed at chance (0.49-0.50). At the default threshold of 0.50, elastic net logistic regression was the best classifier (sensitivity 0.56, positive predictive value 0.64). At 0.12 (near the outcome prevalence), the SVM detected all cases (negative predictive value 1.00), but positive predictive values were low for all models (0.13-0.26). Decision-curve analysis favored most models over treat-all and treat-none lines at thresholds between 0.05 and 0.25. Baseline survey items, mainly on functional impairment, had the largest feature importance. Conclusions: Compact classical models performed as well as transformers, which were considerably more computationally intensive. Decision-curve analysis supports further clinical exploration of these tools for triaging daily psychological distress, though our results suggest the relative value of psychosocial assessments and digital data should be carefully analyzed. External validation is needed before clinical use.
nf53a07c3f08b: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) is a recognized precursor of myeloid malignancy and an independent cardiovascular risk factor, but its relationship with solid tumors is incompletely defined, particularly at histologic resolution. Here, we quantify the association between CHIP and incident cancer across hematologic and solid-organ sites, by clone size, mutation number, and histologic subtype in a prospective cohort of UK Biobank participants with baseline genetic sequencing and cancer ascertained by national registry linkage; those with pre-baseline cancer were excluded. Vanderbilt BioVU was used for replication. CHIP was associated with any incident cancer (HR, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.18-1.27) and with all solid tumors combined (HR, 1.13; 95% CI, 1.08-1.19). Among 17 endpoints, two survived multiple testing correction: lung adenocarcinoma (HR, 1.79; 95% CI, 1.48 - 2.16) and esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (HR, 2.28; 95% CI, 1.37-3.81). Risk increased with clone size and multi-hit CHIP, most markedly for esophageal cancer (VAF [≥]30%: HR, 2.72), and the esophageal squamous association persisted in 5-year landmark analysis (HR, 2.57). In BioVU, CHIP was directionally associated with esophageal cancer and lung adenocarcinoma and its association with all solid tumors overall (HR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.17-1.32) was confirmed. These findings extend CHIP from a hematologic and cardiovascular risk marker to a risk marker of solid-organ cancer risk with histologic resolution and motivate clone-size aware risk models and mechanistic studies.
n9e78cbba638f: Background: Rotator cuff-related shoulder pain accounts for up to 85% of shoulder pain. Guidelines recommend 6 months of non-surgical care before considering surgery, yet many are referred to a surgeon before trying it. High referral rates to public hospital shoulder surgery clinics in Australia mean many patients wait 1-2 years to see a surgeon, during which symptoms may become more complex and costly to manage. A promising solution is the VIRtual physiotherapist-led Triage of referrals to shoUlder surgEons (VIRTUE) model of care, in which physiotherapists screen new referrals and determine suitability for non-surgical care or surgical review. However, no such model has been co-designed to incorporate virtual care nor evaluated in a randomised controlled trial. Aims: The broad aim of this study is to co-design the VIRTUE model of care ready for evaluation in a randomised controlled trial conducted in public hospital shoulder surgery clinics in Australia. Specifically, this study has two aims (two stages): i) explore stakeholders perceptions of the feasibility, acceptability and implementation of the VIRTUE model of care for adults with rotator cuff-related shoulder pain who are referred to public hospital shoulder surgery clinics; and ii) co-design the VIRTUE model of care so that it is user-centred and acceptable to patients, clinicians and key stakeholders. Methods: Stage 1 is a qualitative descriptive study using semi-structured online interviews with patients, clinicians and key stakeholders, recruited using purposive, maximum variation sampling. Interviews will explore experiences of current care, perceptions of the proposed model, and barriers and facilitators to implementation, guided by the Theoretical Framework for Acceptability and Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research. Stage 2 will use Experience-Based Co-Design methodology and involves three online workshops: separate workshops for patients, and for clinicians and key stakeholders, then a combined workshop. Workshops will explore Stage 1 findings, perceptions of the proposed model, and refinements needed to finalise it, with data mapped to the Framework for Reporting Adaptations and Modifications-Expanded. Conclusion: Co-designing VIRTUE with patients, clinicians and key stakeholders will ensure it is user-centred, acceptable and feasible within Australian public health services, ready for evaluation in a randomised controlled trial. By facilitating timely and equitable access to evidence-based care, VIRTUE could improve outcomes for patients, ensure specialist services are available for those most in need, and improve health system performance.
n190d4debb953: Communication failures are repeatedly implicated in harmful experiences and outcomes in pregnancy care, especially in contexts of loss, yet little is known about how communication itself is represented in the institutional texts that shape expectations of care. This study examines the extent to which communication is discussed, and how patient-healthcare professional interaction is framed, in publicly accessible UK discourse about pregnancy loss. Two corpora comprising texts from seven medical organisations (120,383 words) and eight charities (224,481 words) were divided into healthcare professional-facing and patient-facing sub-corpora. Frequency, semantic keyness, keyword and concordance analyses were conducted using Wmatrix7. In medical discourse, language and communicative interaction were underrepresented, while speech acts associated with unidirectional professional activities such as advising, recommending and referring were overrepresented. Compared with charity texts, medical outputs foregrounded clinical evidence, policy, risk and professional knowledge. Characteristic forms including 'confirmed', 'advised', 'recommended' and 'offered' frequently occurred in passive or agentless constructions that positioned patients principally as recipients of information; patient agency was most visible in 'reporting' symptoms or concerns. Charity discourse more often foregrounded talking, listening, feelings, preferences, wording, lived experience, and patient knowledge; representing communication as active and bidirectional. We argue that UK medical discourse constructs communication primarily as the transmission of authorised knowledge rather than as relational clinical practice, reinforcing a paternalistic distribution of communicative agency. Medical institutions should embed listening, reciprocal dialogue, sensitivity to language preferences, and checks on understanding as core standards of safe pregnancy care.
n2bb88287d2c0: Objective This study evaluated whether patient-specific digital twins integrating 3D aortic anatomy and structural wall stress could identify patients with acute uncomplicated type B aortic dissection (AUTBAD) at high risk for adverse aortic events. Methods We analyzed CTAs from 50 patients extracted from a 400 AUTBAD patient database treated with optimal medical therapy from 1999-2025. Digital twin models were constructed, and statistical shape modeling and reduced-order fluid-structure interaction analysis were performed. Anatomic shape and biomechanical stress data were integrated into models predicting freedom from aortic events, defined as intervention or aortic-related death, using leave-one-out cross-validation. A cross-validated risk score was generated for each patient, with higher scores indicating higher event risk. Results At diagnosis, the median descending aortic diameter was 40.61 mm. During follow-up, 35 patients experienced an aortic event: 28 interventions (56%) and 7 aortic-related deaths (14%). Stratification by descending aortic diameter above or below 40.61 mm yielded higher- versus lower-risk aortic event-free survival of 72.0% versus 84.0% at 1 year and 27.8% versus 56.7% at 6 years (p=0.035; C-index=0.590). In the cross-validated multidimensional model combining morphology and structural stress, higher- versus lower-risk event-free survival was 60.0% versus 96.0% at 1 year and 12.5% versus 68.9% at 6 years (p<0.001; C-index=0.792). Conclusions Digital twin modeling integrating morphology and wall stress provided greater risk separation than univariable predictors in AUTBAD patients. With independent validation, patient-specific AUTBAD risk stratification using geometric and biomechanical data may ultimately contribute to identification of high-risk patients who may benefit from early endovascular repair.
na0d741ff230f: Improved understanding of how myelin damage contributes to disability in multiple sclerosis (MS) is needed to inform targeted therapeutic strategies and improve clinical trial platforms. Magnetization transfer saturation ( MTsat ) and T 1 relaxometry provide in vivo quantitative MRI measures of myelin integrity, and may offer insights into disability-relevant pathology beyond inflammatory relapse. This longitudinal study explores the relationship between early demyelination and disability progression over the first five years following diagnosis. 62 people with relapsing-remitting (pwRR)MS (≤ 6 months post-diagnosis, 48 female, mean age 38 years) underwent baseline and one-year MRI and Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) assessment. At five-year follow-up, 56/62 (90.3%) completed EDSS and 40/62 additionally completed MRI (64.5%). Disability progression was defined as an increase of ≥ 1.5, ≥ 1.0 or ≥ 0.5 points for a previous EDSS score of < 1.0, 1.0 to 5.5, and ≥ 6.0, respectively. Baseline neurofilament light chain (NfL), glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), and EBNA1 immunoglobulin (IgG) titres were also measured. MTsat was calculated within normal-appearing white matter (NAWM), white matter lesions (WML), cortical and deep grey matter (GM) structures. Associations between change in MTsat and disability progression were assessed with binomial logistic regression. Interactions with interval disease activity (i.e. new/enlarging lesions [NELs]) were investigated, and comparisons were made with healthy control test-retest data (n = 11). Exploratory analyses were performed for: (prolonged) T 1 ; baseline metrics; blood-derived markers; diffusion-weighted imaging; and, disability-associated differences in five-year microstructural MRI trajectories. Greater baseline-to-one-year decreases in NAWM and WML MTsat were associated with baseline-to-one-year disability progression (adjusted odds ratio [95% confidence interval] = 0.255 [0.078 to 0.602] and 0.261 [0.084 to 0.638]; false discovery rate [FDR]-corrected p -value = 0.015 and 0.015). NELs did not influence these associations (interaction p -values > 0.05). One-to-five-year changes in MTsat were not associated with one-to-five-year disability progression (FDR-corrected p -values > 0.05). Neither baseline nor baseline-to-one-year MTsat changes predicted future disability progression. No exploratory analyses reached FDR-corrected statistical significance. We show for the first time that progressive NAWM and WML demyelination measured with MTsat is associated with early disability progression in recently diagnosed RRMS, independent of radiological inflammatory disease activity. Neither MTsat nor T 1 are associated with longer-term progression over the subsequent four years. MTsat is sensitive to disability-relevant demyelination not visible on conventional MRI, indicates a potential early window of therapeutic opportunity in the year following diagnosis, and is a promising clinically applicable disease stratifier and surrogate endpoint for therapeutic trials.
n0ce994c84c08: Background Uganda continues to experience a high burden of maternal and child morbidity and mortality, partly due to suboptimal utilization and quality of reproductive, maternal, newborn, and child health services. To address these challenges, the Ministry of Health of Uganda, with World Bank funding, implemented results-based financing (RBF) through the Uganda Reproductive, Maternal, and Child Health Services Improvement Project (URMCHIP) in selected districts. Although RBF has been implemented for nearly a decade, evidence on its impact on maternal and child health service indicators in Uganda remains limited. This study assessed the effect of RBF on selected maternal and child health indicators in Mayuge District, Uganda. Methods We retrospectively reviewed the records between July 2018 and June 2019 as the pre-intervention period, July 2019 to June 2021 as the intervention period, and July 2021 to June 2023 as the post-intervention period. We conducted multiple-group interrupted time-series analyses to compare trends in selected maternal and child health indicators between four intervention and three non-intervention health facilities. Results After the implementation of RBF, the number of births in the intervention facilities increased by 1.67 births per month (95% CI [0.19, 3.16]) as compared to the control facilities. The number of women receiving modern family planning methods in intervention facilities increased by 34.1 women per month (CI [25.8, 42.4] as compared to the control facilities. The number of children under five years seen at the outpatient department slightly decreased by -0.24 children per month (CI [-9.58, 9.10]). There was a decline in facility-based births and the number of clients receiving modern family planning methods following the discontinuation of results-based financing in the intervention health facilities. Conclusions There was an improvement in selected maternal and child health indicators in the intervention health facilities following the implementation of RBF, with a subsequent decline in facility-based births and the number of clients receiving modern family planning methods after RBF was discontinued. We recommend that policymakers consider allocating additional funds towards RBF to improve health service delivery.
n37e7a4e8ec1c: Neurosurgery is an effective treatment for drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE), but its success depends on the accurate delineation of the epileptogenic focus, approximated noninvasively by electric and magnetic source imaging (ESI/MSI) of high-density electroencephalography (HD-EEG) and magnetoencephalography (MEG). These modalities have distinct sensitivity profiles; consequently, epileptiform activity detected by one modality may remain undetected by the other. However, the implications of these differences for spike detectability and localization accuracy, and the added value of combined electromagnetic source imaging (EMSI), remain insufficiently characterized under clinically realistic conditions. Here, we characterize HD-EEG and MEG sensitivity profiles and compare ESI, MSI, and EMSI, using realistic simulations with known ground truth. We generated HD-EEG and MEG datasets from cortical, insular, and hippocampal sources across multiple orientations, activated using patient-derived intracranial EEG spike waveforms. Spike sensitivity and localization accuracy were evaluated using dipole scanning, dynamic statistical parametric mapping (dSPM), and linearly constrained minimum variance (LCMV). EEG demonstrated higher spike detection rates and sensitivity for radially cortical sources at gyral crowns and sulcal bottoms (p<0.001), while MEG detected more spikes from tangential cortical sources along sulcal walls (p<0.001). MSI localized tangential sources more accurately than ESI across all methods (p<0.001), while dipole scanning outperformed dSPM and LCMV for cortical and insular sources (p<0.001). EMSI outperformed ESI (p<0.001) but did not improve localization over MSI. These findings suggest that complementary anatomical sensitivities of HD-EEG and MEG may improve epileptogenic source characterization, supporting simultaneous acquisition during the presurgical evaluation of patients with DRE.
n1ac2cb3255c1: Background: Diet may be associated with depression, but evidence on locally consumed food groups in Indonesia is limited. Objectives: To compare food-group intake between people with and without a formal diagnosis of depression in Tangerang, Indonesia, and to explore whether BMI modifies any association. Methods: In this case-control study, cases were psychiatric outpatients with a formal diagnosis of depression. Controls had no formal diagnosis and were recruited through university and community networks. Daily intake of ten food groups was estimated with a semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire. Intakes were compared with independent-samples t-tests (Welch's test when variances were unequal), overall and stratified by BMI group. Logistic regression estimated the odds of depression per 100 g/day of sweetened beverage intake, adjusted for BMI group, sex, and age, with a sweetened beverage and BMI group interaction term. Results: There were 257 participants: 104 cases and 153 controls. Sweetened beverages were the only food group whose intake differed significantly between groups (approximately 214 vs. 153 g/day; mean difference 61 g/day; 95% CI 18-103; p=0.005). Each additional 100 g/day was associated with higher odds of depression after adjustment (OR 1.29; 95% CI 1.09-1.52). The association appeared stronger in underweight/normal-weight participants (ratio of ORs for overweight/obese vs. underweight/normal 0.70; 95% CI 0.49-0.99; p for interaction=0.046). Conclusions: Higher sweetened beverage intake was associated with depression in this sample, and there was modest evidence that the association differed by BMI group. Because the study is cross-sectional in timing, the case-control samples were selected differently, and many comparisons were made, these findings are exploratory. They do not establish causality.
nd6b29081d0f6: Accurate and timely probabilistic dengue forecasts can support public health preparedness, but producing reliable forecasts across locations and time horizons remains challenging. We evaluated five statistical, machine-learning, deep-learning, and foundation-model approaches for forecasting monthly reported dengue cases across 5,570 Brazilian municipalities at 1-, 3-, 6- and 12-month horizons, with forecasts backtested from January 2020 to August 2025. The time-series foundation model TimesFM maintained comparatively stable probabilistic forecast performance at longer horizons, while most other models showed declining performance. We then tested whether spatial representations of human and environmental context from a Population Dynamics Foundation Model (PDFM) could improve forecasts through post-hoc residual adjustment. PDFM adjustment improved mean probabilistic forecast performance, measured by the Weighted Interval Score (WIS), in 19 of 20 model-horizon combinations, although the magnitude and frequency of improvements varied across models, horizons and municipalities. The largest improvements were observed for N-BEATS, including a reduction in mean WIS of 1.13 at the six-month horizon (95% CI [0.84, 1.48]; Diebold-Mariano p < 0.0001), with improvements also observed for XGBoost. The proportion of forecasts improved by PDFM generally increased with locally reported dengue case counts, although this relationship varied between models. Covariate selection, spatial fitting and forecast aggregation strategies showed strong model-dependent effects, while monthly model retraining provided no consistent advantage in the settings evaluated. Together, these findings highlight the potential of pretrained representations for dengue forecasting, with benefits dependent on forecasting architecture, horizon and modelling configuration.
ne33bd84b248a: In 2025, a chikungunya outbreak in southern China resulted in more than 25,000 confirmed cases, but its origins and transmission history remain unresolved. As part of the public health investigation, we generated 1,264 near-complete chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genomes from Guangdong Province and integrated genomic, epidemiological, entomological, and human mobility data to reconstruct the emergence and spread of this outbreak. Our analyses traced the outbreak to a single dominant introduction of a Reunion-associated East/Central/South African (ECSA) virus lineage and dated the origin of the sampled Guangdong outbreak lineage from late April to early May 2025. The interval between the estimated origin of the outbreak lineage and the first reported case was consistent with a period of undetected local transmission and exposed limitations in passive surveillance for early arboviral outbreak detection. Spatiotemporal reconstruction showed two distinct epidemic waves with contrasting transmission dynamics. The Foshan wave involved frequent medium- to long-distance viral movement, while the Jiangmen wave remained relatively localized. Together, these findings reconstruct the early establishment and spatially heterogeneous spread of the largest documented CHIKV epidemic in southern China to date and demonstrate the necessity of expanding active genomic surveillance in areas at the fringe of CHIKV endemic transmission for timely detecting and characterizing emerging epidemics.
ne67a096b21bd: Early-phase trials of candidate malaria interventions in endemic areas often use "time-to-first" infection as a primary efficacy endpoint. This approach does not assess infection risk after the initial infection, and its censoring of trial participants after their first infection can introduce bias by removing more high-risk participants from control than treatment arms over time. Efficacy estimate precision may also decline as risk set size decreases. Here we assessed the utility of genotyping all infections in an intervention trial to determine the total infection incidence in each participant for the full follow-up period. Specifically, we genotyped all Plasmodium falciparum infections detected in a previously-reported phase 2 trial of the antimalarial monoclonal antibody CIS43LS in 330 Malian adults. We determined the molecular force of infection (molFOI; rate of new P. falciparum strains) for each participant, expressing efficacy as the percent molFOI reduction in CIS43LS versus placebo arms (Eff molFOI ). Six-month Eff molFOI was 86.5% (95% CI: 80.1-90.8) and 70.7% (61.0-78.0) for the 40 mg/kg and 10 mg/kg doses, respectively. These estimates are similar to those from time-to-first infection analysis, but more precise when analyzing efficacy by trial-month and when stratifying by P. falciparum infection-status at enrollment. Participants infected at enrollment had lower Eff molFOI and acquired infections earlier in the trial, creating systematic differences in risk composition between arms over time. Genotyping showed no evidence for escape-polymorphisms in the CIS43LS epitope. These results demonstrate how genotypic endpoints can provide a more comprehensive understanding of candidate malaria interventions.
n8f15a36ed4fe: Importance: Rare genetic syndromes are often drivers of complex multimorbidity. However, current methods consider multimorbidity as the sum of chronic diagnoses, which does not account for subthreshold impairment. Objective: To develop a quantitative multimorbidity score (MMS) for rare genetic syndromes that summarizes the neurodevelopmental and psychiatric multimorbidity landscape, including subthreshold symptoms, using 3q29 deletion and 3q29 duplication syndromes as hallmark examples. Design: We developed a multimorbidity metric and applied it to cross-sectional data. Remote phenotyping from 2023-2026. In-person phenotyping from 2017-2020. Setting: Remote phenotyping conducted at Rutgers University. In-person phenotyping conducted at Emory University. Participants: Participants were 6 years of age and older. 3q29del and 3q29dup recruited from the 3q29 registry and direct referrals and contacts. Syndrome status confirmed by genetic report review. Typically developing controls recruited from community sources and ResearchMatch. Main Outcomes and Measures: We developed a quantitative MMS across five distinct domains of functioning, operationalized as the sum of z-scores across six standardized assessments. The MMS was calculated for each study participant and compared across groups. Within 3q29del, we evaluated the relationship between MMSs and Vineland-3 adaptive behavior. Results: 96 individuals with 3q29del (52.08% male, 18.01+/-11.47 years old), 28 individuals with 3q29dup (50.00% male, 20.82+/-13.64 years old), and 53 controls (41.51% male, 17.77+/-10.74 years old) were included. 3q29del and 3q29dup participants had significantly lower MMS scores compared to controls (3q29del mean=-8.22+/-4.67, 3q29dup mean=-6.47+/-4.66, control mean=1.36+/-2.35, 3q29del p<2E-16, 3q29dup p=4.89E-16). Within 3q29del, subjects with more severe multimorbidity had greater impairment in adaptive behavior (R2=0.589, p<2E-16). The quantitative MMS is more highly correlated with adaptive behavior than traditional diagnosis-based multimorbidity metrics (quantitative MMS R2=0.589, diagnosis-based multimorbidity R2=0.447). In a subset of 24 3q29del participants with longitudinal data (58.33% male, 13.17+/-9.08 years old at first evaluation, average time to follow up=5.17+/-0.87 years), the MMS is stable over time (R2=0.858, p=8.34E-8). Conclusions and Relevance: Our novel quantitative MMS is an improved metric for measuring psychiatric multimorbidity in high-risk populations, and accounts for the impact of subthreshold impairments. When applied to 3q29del and 3q29dup, it quantifies the individual burden of multimorbidity, is stable over time, and is associated with clinical outcome measures.
naca72234fe45: Background: Standard body mass index (BMI) categories may understate risk in Asian individuals. Lower Asian action points exist, but their relevance to birth outcomes is unclear. Objectives: To estimate the proportion of normal-weight Asian mothers with BMI 23.0-24.9 kg/m2 and its association with birth outcomes, overall and by Asian subgroup, and to compare Asian and White mothers. Methods: Repeated cross-sectional study of US singleton live births, 2016-2023 (National Vital Statistics System). Outcomes were hypertensive disorders, caesarean delivery, preterm birth, and low birthweight. Modified Poisson regression, adjusted for confounders and Asian subgroup, estimated risk ratios (RRs), standardized risks, and risk differences (RDs). We tested for a change in slope at 23.0 kg/m2, subgroup heterogeneity, and race x BMI interaction. Results: Among 1,758,116 non-Hispanic Asian mothers, 314,510 (17.9%) had BMI 23.0-24.9 kg/m2, 30.4% of normal-weight mothers. Compared with BMI 18.5-22.9, standardized risk of hypertensive disorders was 4.5% versus 3.2% (RD 1.4 percentage points, 95% CI 1.3, 1.5; RR 1.44, 95% CI 1.40, 1.47), and of caesarean delivery 32.4% versus 28.6% (RR 1.14, 95% CI 1.13, 1.14). Preterm birth risk was 7.2% versus 6.6% (RR 1.08, 95% CI 1.06, 1.10); low birthweight risk was not higher (7.1% versus 7.5%; RR 0.95, 95% CI 0.93, 0.97). The hypertensive-disorder slope showed no evidence of change at 23.0 (ratio of per-unit RRs 0.99, 95% CI 0.98, 1.01); the hypertensive-disorder RR ranged from 1.24 (95% CI 1.18, 1.29) among Asian Indian to 1.70 (95% CI 1.60, 1.81) among Chinese mothers. BMI-outcome associations differed between Asian and White mothers. Conclusions: Nearly one in three normal-weight Asian mothers had BMI 23.0-24.9 kg/m2, associated with higher risks of hypertensive disorders and caesarean delivery but not low birthweight. The hypertensive-disorder gradient showed no evidence of change at 23.0 kg/m2, and associations varied across Asian subgroups.
na50532cf4d97: The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) remains the standard metric for assessing obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity, although it does not fully capture the physiological consequences of respiratory events. Hypoxic burden (HB), which integrates the frequency, depth, and duration of oxygen desaturations, has been proposed as a more comprehensive measure of OSA-related hypoxic stress. This study compared the prognostic value of HB and AHI for subjective and objective treatment outcomes in patients undergoing continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy. Data from 412 patients with OSA who underwent diagnostic and CPAP-treated polysomnography were analyzed, including 52 patients with available follow-up questionnaires. HB was calculated using a validated event-based algorithm. Multivariable regression models were used to predict patient-reported outcomes and changes in sleep architecture, adjusted for age, sex and body mass index. HB consistently demonstrated stronger associations with symptomatic outcomes than AHI. Models including HB showed improved model fit and explained variance. HB remained independently associated with lower follow-up fatigue and better sleep quality after adjustment for AHI. In contrast, AHI was the dominant predictor of objective sleep architecture improvements, including increases in N3 sleep, reductions in N1 sleep, and reductions in arousal index. HB provided additional independent information only for changes in arousal burden. These findings suggest that HB and AHI capture complementary dimensions of OSA severity. While AHI primarily reflects sleep fragmentation and physiological response to CPAP, HB appears more closely related to subjective treatment benefit. Incorporating HB alongside AHI may improve clinical phenotyping and prediction of treatment response in OSA.
n4190dcdcbae2: Introduction: Treatment strategies for colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRLM) are increasingly complex, driving interest in advanced prognostic tools. Externally validated benchmarks based on established clinical risk scores are needed to contextualise emerging models. However, existing scores remain difficult to apply and compare, because they provide categorical risk strata rather than individualised probabilities, and because model parameters are rarely published. Here, we validate and recalibrate seven established risk scores to derive individualised recurrence probabilities for future score benchmarking. Method: Patients undergoing index CRLM resection from two tertiary centres were included: Karolinska University Hospital (retrospective KaroLiver cohort [2013-2021, follow-up to 2025, n=709]) and Oslo University Hospital (OSLO-COMET trial cohort [2012-2016, follow-up to 2022, n=198]). Performance of the GAME, m-CS, Fong, Nordlinger, Nagashima, Konopke and Helsinki scores was assessed using recurrence-free survival as the primary outcome. Results: Among 709 patients in KaroLiver (median age 67 years [IQR 59-74]; 434 men [61%]), 422 (60%) had synchronous metastases and 444 (63%) received neoadjuvant chemotherapy. All scores significantly stratified recurrence risk (log-rank P<0.001; time-dependent AUC 0.63-0.74 at 3 years), albeit with performance differences across time points. Recalibrated models showed good agreement between predicted and observed recurrence and were externally validated in OSLO-COMET with broadly comparable net benefit. Models were implemented in the online tool PLATO (Personalised Liver metastases risk AssessmenT in Oncology). Conclusion: Established CRLM risk scores can be translated into individualised probabilistic recurrence estimates at clinically relevant time points, supporting patient communication, risk-adapted surveillance and transparent benchmarking of next-generation prognostic models.
n2f735c0957aa: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Improper refuse disposal remains an environmental health concern in many Nigerian communities. This study assessed knowledge, attitudes and practices relating to refuse disposal among adult residents of Okelele community, Ilorin East Local Government Area, Kwara State, Nigeria. METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional community-based study was conducted among 180 adults. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire covering sociodemographic characteristics, knowledge, attitudes and disposal practices. Descriptive statistics summarised responses, and chi-square tests assessed associations between categorical variables at a 5% significance level. RESULTS: Of 180 respondents, 102 (56.7%) had good knowledge, while 87 (48.3%) had negative attitudes and 99 (55.0%) had poor refuse-disposal practices. Commonly reported practices included incineration (50.6%), disposal into drains (30.6%) and open burning (21.7%). Absence of waste containers (37.2%) and distance to available containers (28.9%) were the leading reported barriers. Knowledge was associated with practice (chi-square=22.122; p<0.001) and attitude (chi-square=8.221; p=0.016); practice was also associated with attitude (chi-square=5.970; p=0.015). CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS FOR TRANSLATION: Despite generally good knowledge, poor disposal practices were common. Improving access to reliable waste-collection infrastructure, alongside community education and enforcement of local waste-management measures, may help translate knowledge into safer practices. Keywords: Solid waste; Waste management; Knowledge; Attitude; Health behavior; Nigeria
n2d50796781b5: Background: Chloramphenicol, tetracycline, zinc oxide (CTZ) paste has been widely used, particularly in Latin America, in Lesion Sterilization and Tissue Repair (LSTR) procedures in primary molars. However, reports on its long-term efficacy are scarce. Aim: This multicentre non-inferiority randomised trial compared the efficacy of LSTR using CTZ paste with conventional zinc oxide-eugenol (ZOE) pulpectomy in primary molars. Design: 199 primary molars from children aged 3 to 9 years were randomised to the CTZ or ZOE groups. The primary outcome was clinical and radiographic success at 24 months. Clinical time, children's behaviour, immediate discomfort and postoperative pain were also evaluated. The main analysis followed the intention-to-treat (ITT) principle, comparing success proportions with the Miettinen-Nurminen method, considering a prespecified non-inferiority margin of 15% (p < 0.05). Results: Overall success rates in the ITT population were 64.3% for CTZ and 58.7% for ZOE, with a difference of 5.6% (95% CI: -9.3 to 20.4; p<0.01). Mean; standard deviation clinical time was significantly shorter in CTZ (36.3; 9.8 min) than in ZOE (63.0; 16.3 min) (p<0.01). Children's behaviour, immediate discomfort and postoperative pain were similar between groups (p>0.05). Conclusion: LSTR with CTZ paste was non-inferior to conventional ZOE pulpectomy after 24 months of follow-up.
n6d9c43f326e9: This study is part of the AI4Food project, which aims to identify the physiological and behavioral factors influencing weight variation in overweight and obese individuals through integrative analysis of multi-source data. A 30-day crossover intervention was conducted on 93 participants at IMDEA Nutrition Institute, combining a traditional phase (questionnaires, food diaries) and a digital phase (Fitbit Sense Smartwatch, FreeStyle Libre 2 glucose sensor). The collected data encompassed sleep, glucose, skin temperature, nutrition, and gut microbiome information. After rigorous preprocessing and alignment by intervention days, unsupervised clustering, association analysis, and machine learning models were applied to uncover physiological patterns linked to weight dynamics. Results showed greater weight reduction during the digital phase in Group 2, while between-group differences were not significant. Significant associations were observed between nocturnal respiratory rate, skin temperature, and weight variation. Under participant-level five-fold cross-validation, Random Forest models achieved mean accuracies of 64.3% for thermoregulation and 61.7% for glucose phenotype prediction, with RMSSD, restlessness, and nocturnal respiratory rate among the most influential predictors. In contrast, microbiome composition remained almost stable over the short intervention period. These findings support the potential of AI-driven integration of wearable and nutritional data to stratify metabolic phenotypes and advance personalized nutrition strategies in obesity management.
n45cd98efcb03: Introduction: Dementia and late-life depression are rising rapidly in sub-Saharan Africa, yet prevention frameworks remain focused on individual behaviour. Multidimensional poverty is a plausible structural determinant of brain health but is rarely assessed. Methods: This cross-sectional analysis of the community-based Akili Mali study assessed adults aged 60 years and older in three rural communities in Kilimanjaro, Tanzania. Outcomes were the 15-item Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS-15), IDEA cognitive screen, CERAD ten-word list, and verbal fluency. Deprivation was measured with a nine-indicator Alkire-Foster Multidimensional Deprivation Index. Missing data were multiply imputed; models adjusted for age, sex, education, community, comorbidity, and health behaviours. Results: Of 1054 participants (mean age 70.2 years [SD 9.35]; 629 [59.7%] women), 840 (81.9%) of 1026 were multidimensionally deprived. Each unit increase in deprivation score predicted a higher GDS-15 score ({beta} 4.83, 95% CI 3.82 to 5.83), higher odds of screen-positive depression (odds ratio 17.18, 6.89 to 42.83), lower IDEA score ({beta} -1.97, -2.97 to -0.97), and lower verbal fluency ({beta} -2.57, -3.77 to -1.36; all p<0.001). CERAD measures and self-reported impairment showed no association. At community level this gradient inverted: the most deprived community had the lowest depression and highest cognition, yet perceived social standing did not differ. Conclusion: Multidimensional deprivation was near-universal and independently associated with worse brain health. The community-level inversion, with perceived social standing equivalent across communities of unequal material circumstances, indicates that absolute deprivation alone does not explain the distribution of brain health. Relative position and community resilience are priorities for study
nf03f987c7a40: Interictal epileptiform discharges, so called spikes, are often strongly activated during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep in childhood epilepsies. In children with pronounced spike activation during NREM - sleep, spike burden can be associated with lifelong impaired cognitive functions. This spike activation is also related to alterations in sleep oscillations, specifically slow waves and spindles, which play essential roles in brain maintenance and maturation. These observations suggest that spikes may disrupt sleep-dependent brain processes that are critical for the development of cognitive functions. Phase-targeted auditory stimulation during NREM sleep delivers brief, non-arousing tones at specific phases of ongoing slow waves to modulate sleep oscillations. Recently, our group showed that isolated, less frequent, and thus less expected, tones engage widespread thalamocortical networks, whereas repetitive, regular trains of tones promote habituation and engage more local corticocortical networks. In this study, we use these contrasting stimulation patterns for a targeted modulation of sleep oscillations and examine their interaction with epileptic spikes. In an initial exploratory study (N = 10; age range: 7.3 - 16.2 years), we used a within-night block design to directly compare responses to the different stimulation patterns. Isolated tones delivered at long interstimulus intervals induced a transient increase in spike rate, whereas down-phase stimulation delivered in trains at short, regular intervals was associated with a significant reduction. We subsequently optimized the train-based paradigm and evaluated stimulation delivered throughout the night in a proof-of-concept study using a counterbalanced, between-night design (N = 5; age range: 4.4 - 10.7 years). Spike density decreased locally in all patients, providing convergent evidence for the effects observed in the exploratory study. With this mechanistically guided approach, we demonstrate that repetitive down-phase auditory stimulation of slow waves results in a local reduction of epileptic spikes. This framework may provide a rational basis for targeted interventions aimed at reducing spikes and related cognitive impairments.
n59d76b51d940: The generalizability of FDA-cleared Lumipulse plasma pTau217 / A{beta}42 ratio cutpoints to Asian populations remains uncertain, especially in those with high burden of concomitant cerebrovascular disease (CeVD). We evaluated pTau217, A{beta}42 and their ratio in 205 Singapore-based participants with corresponding amyloid neuroimaging. In-house cutpoints were derived using a three-range strategy targeting 95% sensitivity and specificity. Plasma pTau217/A{beta}42 ratio outperformed pTau217 alone (area under the curve, 0.951 versus 0.925; p=0.004), with comparable performance across CeVD severities. Plasma ratio cutpoints achieved 98% negative predictive value, 88% positive predictive value, and 95% accuracy, classifying 10% as intermediate-risk. Using FDA-cleared cutpoints for our cohort retained 97% sensitivity and negative predictive value but yielded lower specificity (86%), positive predictive value (77%) and accuracy (85%), with 29% classified as intermediate-risk. Our findings support the need for population-specific validation of cutpoints from FDA-cleared blood biomarkers of brain amyloid pathology.
n4fa458e5f9e3: The development of biologically targeted therapeutics (BTTs) that slow Parkinson's disease progression has been hampered by a reliance on testing interventions in clinically defined populations with already advanced pathobiology. Publications on the biological definition and classification of neuronal a-synuclein disease (NSD), and the development of the NSD integrated staging system (NSD-ISS), have generated a framework for identifying individuals with NSD prior to the emergence of a clinically defined syndrome. Path to Prevention (P2P) is a phase 2A, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled platform trial designed to assess the safety and efficacy of interventions in an early-stage NSD population. The trial is embedded within the observational Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative (PPMI), a structure that enables recruitment of participants from the PPMI cohort, leverages existing operational infrastructure, and utilizes data from non-P2P enrolled PPMI participants in the Bayesian statistical modeling. P2P will enroll participants at least 60 years of age with NSD Stage 2B (abnormal ⍺-synuclein, dopaminergic dysfunction, and prodromal signs or symptoms without functional impairment) without a clinically defined diagnosis of PD or a related disorder. As a platform trial, P2P will enable the testing of multiple interventions under a Master Protocol at approximately 35 sites across North America and Europe. Interventions are selected from industry-submitted applications based on biological relevance of the targets, and on the adequacy of the safety data appropriate to the target population. Each treatment regimen will have 125 participants on active treatment and at least 125 shared placebo control participants. Participants will remain on treatment for a maximum of 144 weeks or until 96 weeks since the randomization of the last participant. P2P has two primary endpoints, 1) rate of change in mean putamen specific binding ratio from baseline through follow-up and, 2) rate of change in the MDS-UPDRS Part III motor examination from baseline through follow-up or initiation of dopaminergic treatment. A range of secondary and exploratory biomarker-focused endpoints will be assessed. The protocol was developed with input from multiple stakeholders, including people with early-stage NSD, biopharmaceutical industry leaders, and regulatory authorities. P2P is the first trial to test biologically targeted assets in biologically defined prodromal participants utilizing an efficient platform design, which will provide the field with tools to expand therapeutic development, and enable intervention at earlier stages of neurodegeneration. P2P is scheduled to begin enrollment in December 2026 and is committed to data sharing and broad dissemination of learnings from the study.
n61b512d9601c: Background: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide. Diet plays a key role in CVD prevention while linking human health with environmental sustainability. The EAT-Lancet Commission proposed the Planetary Health Diet (PHD), a predominantly plant-based dietary pattern emphasizing high-quality foods and reduced meat consumption. Despite growing interest in the PHD, no randomized controlled trial (RCT) has evaluated its effects using the PHD index on established and novel cardiometabolic biomarkers. Methods: The PlanetDiet study is a six-month, three-arm parallel RCT investigating the effects of sustainable diets on traditional and novel cardiometabolic risk factors in 180 Danish adults aged 45?70 years at high cardiovascular risk. Participants are randomized to a PHD, an ovo-lacto-vegetarian diet, or their habitual diet (control). The primary outcome is changes in a composite cardiometabolic health score, with secondary outcomes including changes in metabolomic and proteomic profiles. Clinical assessments include the analysis of urine, blood, and faecal samples; continuous glucose monitoring; anthropometry and body composition measurements; dietary records; and self-reported questionnaires assessing physical activity, quality of life and dietary acceptance. To support adherence, participants receive four individualized dietary counselling sessions, two group sessions, seasonal food boxes tailored to their assigned diet, and access to a personalized digital application with recipes, individualized timelines, and visit scheduling. Conclusions: PlanetDiet will provide evidence on the effects of sustainable dietary patterns on cardiometabolic health. It will also investigate molecular pathways linking diet to cardiometabolic disease. Ultimately, the study may inform the development of effective, personalized dietary interventions that promote both human and planetary health. Trial registration: Sustainable Diets and Cardiometabolic Health (PlanetDiet): NCT07189676 [ClinicalTrials.gov] [registered before inclusion start; 2025-09-15]; Unique identifier: H-25030722.
n2d425dfcfbc1: Objective: Early progression to insulin following initial management as type 2 diabetes may indicate missed type 1 diabetes. Recent guidelines advise islet-autoantibody testing in all adults who progress to insulin within 3 years, though this has not been directly tested. We aimed to determine whether positive islet autoantibodies in this setting confirm the genetic characteristics and C-peptide progression of classical type 1 diabetes. Research Design and Methods: We compared genetic susceptibility to type 1 and type 2 diabetes (T1DGRS and T2DGRS) and prospectively assessed C-peptide loss over 3 years after diagnosis among islet-autoantibody-positive adults initially treated as having type 2 diabetes (without insulin) who progressed to insulin within 3 years (n=86), versus participants with classical type 1 (n=499) and type 2 (n=603) diabetes. Results were replicated in cross-sectional data from the DARE/GoDARTS studies (n=9466). Results: Participants who progressed to insulin within 3 years and had positive islet autoantibodies had the genetic characteristics and C-peptide loss of classical type 1 diabetes: T1DGRS -0.04 (-0.27, 0.18) vs 0.00 (-0.09, 0.09) [p=0.71], T2DGRS -0.35 (-0.59, -0.11) vs -0.35 (-0.44, -0.26) [p=0.99] and annual change in urine C-peptide creatinine ratio -47% (-55%, -40%) vs -49% (-52%, -46%) [p=0.6] respectively. In contrast, autoantibody-positive participants without early insulin (n=51) had genetic and C-peptide characteristics consistent with type 2 diabetes. Findings were similar in cross-sectional cohorts. Conclusion: Islet-autoantibody-positive individuals with early insulin requirement following initial treatment as type 2 diabetes have similar genotype and progression to classical type 1 diabetes. This supports recent guidance that they should be diagnosed and treated as type 1 diabetes.
n2fe4b654ea85: Objective: To describe how people use the unapproved peptides BPC-157 and TB-500 for tendon, ligament and muscle injury and what side effects they report. Methods: Using a large language model validated against physician review, we analyzed 92,254 posts and comments from 28,652 users in Reddit's peptide communities from 2021 to 2026. We compared side effects with those reported by users of four other peptides in the same communities. Results: In all, 5,588 users described using BPC-157 and/or TB-500 for a specific musculoskeletal injury, most often a chronic tendon problem of the shoulder, knee or elbow. Only 3.8% of users described physician involvement, and 90.9% of those naming a source bought from research-chemical vendors. The median BPC-157 dose (366 mcg per injection) was about 2.7 times the human-equivalent dose of the 10 mcg/kg rat regimen, and among new users it rose from 300 mcg in 2024 to 500 mcg in 2025. Of those stating an outcome, 79.3% reported improvement, and 36.6% of all users were also in physical therapy. Overall, 27.2% described at least one side effect, most often fatigue, anxiety, anhedonia and insomnia. Anhedonia was more common than among users of the four other peptides (10.2% versus 1.3% of those with side effects). Conclusion: Use of these unapproved peptides for musculoskeletal injury is largely unsupervised, relying on grey-market products at self-selected, rising doses without established safety or efficacy.
n0c6e5c3d6914: Background: Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) reduces neonatal mortality and morbidity among preterm and low birthweight (LBW) infants, but implementation and quality vary across sub-Saharan African (SSA) hospitals. This study reports KMC coverage and quality of care for preterm and LBW neonates admitted to hospitals in the NEST360 Alliance (Kenya, Malawi, Tanzania, Nigeria) and examines the association between KMC provision and survival to discharge.
